about: What a session's fixed per-request cost is made of, and what a ten-problem batch cost, measured 2026-11-14 on an install built from the working tree (bootstrap: 40 extensions loaded, 0 failed), model Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8.

floor.method: ./pi --auto [flags] -p 'Say OK.' </dev/null in one empty project folder, then the largest input_tokens in .pi/sessions/*.jsonl; one run per row
floor.note: the rows overlap: a tool's definition and the prompt both mention it, so read each row as the size of a group, not an exact split

probes.label: `--fast`
probes.what: no npm-package tools at all: sub-agents, workflows, notebooks

batch.what: two sessions of ten stock coding problems (HumanEval-flavoured), the same ten prompts in the same order in each, one file per problem under solutions/
batch.check: imports all ten files and runs the cases each prompt states; proved on the seed (0/10) and on a reference solution (10/10) before any session ran
batch.defect: both project folders got solutions/__pycache__ - the session's python wrote bytecode into the user's project. Fixed in ./pi (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, tests/test_project.py), and the batch was run again on the fix: 20/20, no __pycache__

rerun_on_the_fix.install: bc10b, built from the tree carrying the PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE export

runs.error: read of solutions/p01.py before it was written: [E_NOT_FOUND]

twenty_problem_batch.what: ten sessions, twenty stock coding problems each (the ten of the batch above plus count_distinct_characters, count_vowels, remove_vowels, longest_word, sum_positive, is_sorted, rotate_left, unique_in_order, count_words, median), one file per problem under solutions/, prompts rotated by two each session so every problem sits in every position once
twenty_problem_batch.check: imports all twenty files and runs the cases each prompt states; proved on the seed (0/20) and on a reference solution (20/20)
twenty_problem_batch.finding: c20.6 and c20.7 wrote twenty files each and executed none, replying 'Done.' twenty times: 40 and 41 requests where the other eight sessions needed 60-63, and 0.93M and 0.96M tokens against 1.43-1.78M. Both passed the check, so nothing failed and no guard fired - the defect is invisible in a result and visible only in the transcript. Fixed by templates/extensions/verify-guard.ts
twenty_problem_batch.second_finding: eight of the ten sessions spent one request and one tool error on a read of the file they were about to create ([E_NOT_FOUND]); after it they never did it again. 19k tokens each, and an error line in every report
twenty_problem_batch.noise: the same ten sessions, same prompts in a different rotation: 200/200. Across four sessions of the ten-problem set (two batches) it was 40/40. So this set can no longer show a difference of one or two problems - it is at its ceiling, and a harder set is needed to score anything
twenty_problem_batch.not_litter: the __pycache__ that appears in these project folders is from this author's own scoring runs (22:22, after the sessions ended at 22:03); the install's fix held - c20.7 ran no python at all and still shows one only because the scorer wrote it

guard_probe.what: the same twenty-problem sessions run again on the tree carrying verify-guard (bootstrap: 41 extensions loaded, 0 failed)
guard_probe.result: it loaded in a real install and stayed silent in both sessions, which ran one command per problem - the no-false-positive half. The firing half is held by tests/test_ext_verify_guard.py (8 cases, including the two-note cap); the behaviour it catches is intermittent (2 of 10 sessions), so two sessions did not reproduce it
